notes: context: Go's cancellation tree on std threads/condvars (event driven, one lazy timer thread). Context is a concrete handle; constructors are methods (Context::background, ctx.with_cancel()) (custom Context implementations are not supported); deadlines are Instants; Done is a handle with wait/wait_timeout/receiver; keys are typed Key<T>. AfterFunc firing order among siblings is unspecified (as in Go). Rust adds Context::check as a convenience.

AfterFunc.note: Each f runs in its own std thread; the returned StopFunc has Go's bool result.

Canceled.note: Error::Canceled; timeout()/temporary() report false (Go's error has no such methods).

Context.note: A concrete clonable handle, not an interface: a user-defined Context implementation cannot be passed where Go accepts one, and parents are always this crate's own contexts. Supporting it needs a trait for custom contexts plus a watcher thread per child (Go's propagateCancel goroutine).

Context.Done.note: Returns a Done handle (wait, wait_timeout, is_done, receiver) instead of a channel; its mpsc receiver reports Disconnected once done.

Context.Value.note: Typed Key<T> (unique, named or type-identified) instead of an untyped any key; returns Option<Arc<T>>.

DeadlineExceeded.note: Error::DeadlineExceeded with timeout() and temporary() both true, as Go's deadlineExceededError.
